data_section_full_text:
The sample is selected from banks listed in the 1997 Bank COMPUSTAT annual
data files. Data on nonperforming loans for the period 1980–97 are obtained from
Keefe, Bruyette, and Woods (KBW). Table 1 reports the effects of the sample
selection criteria on sample size. Merging the COMPUSTAT and KBW data bases
and differencing results in a sample of 1,048 (82 banks) bank-year observations for
which we have complete data. We manually collect nonperforming loan data from
call reports and from the FDIC website to arrive at the final sample of 1,104 (105
banks) bank-year observations.

We require estimates of intrinsic value to test the signaling hypothesis. These
intrinsic value estimates, which are used to calculate the under/over valuation for
each bank, require forecasts of earnings and growth in book value of equity. We
use forecast data from Value Line. Of the 1,104 observations, 847 bank-year observations do not have Value Line forecast data. Therefore, we test Hypothesis 1 using
a sample of 257 bank-year observations from a sample of 35 banks. Due to this
substantial reduction in sample size from using Value Line forecast data, we also
employ the book-to-price (B/P) ratio as an alternative under/over valuation measure
and repeat the tests using this classificatory variable ~~.~~ <sup><u>15</u></sup> Although the B/P ratio may
misclassify banks in terms of their propensity to signal, it allows us to increase the
power of the tests of the signaling and joint hypotheses by significantly increasing
the sample size.
